pathway.title: GRAY MEDIA, INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Gray Media's reported covenant leverage of 5.73x total net understates the burden shown by its own earnings. The company's covenant denominator is USD 994 million, an eight-quarter average that includes the third and fourth quarters of the 2024 election year and USD 144 million of acquisition, financing and synergy adjustments; its last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is USD 709 million, and the same net debt of USD 5,696 million is 8.03x on that figure. Both are correct on their own bases and neither is a maintenance test. The mechanism is that incurrence capacity and covenant optics depend on a smoothed, pro forma denominator while cash interest of USD 385 million is paid out of actual earnings. This is Analyst Interpretation over CP-1 figures.

The company's earnings are cyclical and its fee income is eroding at the same time. Retransmission consent was 46% of FY2025 revenue and political advertising 14% of FY2024 revenue and 1% of FY2025, and USD 133 million of the last twelve months; retransmission consent fell 4% in 2025 and 7% in the first half of 2026 on subscriber loss, one station going independent and a satellite blackout between March and May 1, 2026, with network affiliation fees falling faster so that net retransmission revenue rose to USD 292 million from USD 281 million. Network affiliation agreements expire between mid-2027 and December 31, 2028, just before the December 2028 term loan and revolver maturity. The implication is that FY2026 will flatter cash flow, and FY2027 and FY2028 carry the renewal and refinancing risk.

Liquidity is adequate but depleted by the 2026 transactions. Cash fell from USD 368 million to USD 176 million in the first half, after USD 264 million of acquisition spending; revolver availability is USD 745 million; and on July 21, 2026 the company repurchased USD 100 million of 2029 first lien notes and USD 20 million of 2031 notes using cash and an undisclosed revolver draw. Reading two issuer passages together, a first lien net leverage cap of 4.25x applies when the revolver is drawn or more than USD 50 million of letters of credit are uncollateralized; the company reports 2.55x, so a draw outstanding at a quarter-end would activate a test with headroom of about 40% of the denominator (Analyst Interpretation, issuer-described terms only).

The refinancing in 2025 moved debt up the structure. Principal secured by a lien rose to 65.4% of the total at December 31, 2025 and 65.8% at June 30, 2026, from 55.2% at December 31, 2024, with the 10.5% first lien notes due 2029 and the 9.625% second lien notes due 2032 carrying the highest coupons. Coupon arithmetic gives an annual cost of about USD 443 million on the instruments listed, against an issuer estimate of USD 465 million of interest payments over the next twelve months (the coupon sum excludes receivables-facility interest and fees). The implication for creditors is that unsecured noteholders hold USD 2,008 million behind USD 3,859 million of secured debt, and that the cost of debt leaves little earnings cushion; no recovery conclusion is drawn.

Distributions continue ahead of deleveraging. In the first half of 2026 the company paid USD 17 million of common dividends and USD 27 million of preferred dividends, and it used USD 30 million of new first lien debt to repurchase USD 50 million of preferred liquidation value at a USD 20 million discount. The issuer's USD 465 million interest estimate plus USD 83 million of guided 2026 dividends together equal 77.3% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. Class A shareholders hold 51.5% of the votes and the holders are not identified in the pack, so alignment with creditors cannot be assessed beyond the documented actions.

runs.text: Strengths. Gray Media has scale: stations in 117 full-power markets reaching about 37% of US households, with its own count of 78 markets with the top-rated station (Management Language, Nielsen data not verified by the issuer). Its customer and market concentration is low: no advertiser above 5% of broadcast advertising and the largest market, Phoenix, at 5% of revenue (Documentary Fact). Its liquidity is USD 921 million and no principal is due before December 1, 2028, after refinancings that the company says extended maturities beyond the next two political cycles (Documentary Fact; the claim about political cycles is Management Language). The first lien net leverage ratio of 2.55x is well inside the 3.5x incurrence level and the 4.25x cap (Documentary Fact, issuer-reported). The company has reduced debt in the past: USD 520 million of net principal payments in 2024 (Documentary Fact). Net retransmission revenue held at USD 547 million in FY2025 against USD 550 million in FY2024 despite a USD 53 million fall in retransmission fees, because affiliation fees fell USD 50 million (Documentary Fact).

Weaknesses. Gray Media's leverage is 8.28x on last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA and 8.67x in FY2025, against 4.90x in FY2024, and cash interest cover is 1.84x (Documentary Fact, calculated). Its free cash flow is thin: USD 146 million before and USD 59 million after dividends over the last twelve months (calculated). Its earnings swing with the election cycle and with a high fixed-cost base, and Adjusted EBITDA is a release-only management measure (Documentary Fact). Its revenue base faces subscriber erosion and a cluster of affiliation expiries in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact). A growing share of debt is secured, USD 400 million of receivables financing is fully drawn and outside reported debt, and USD 600 million of senior preferred stock carries a cash dividend of about USD 48 million a year and a change-of-control redemption (Analyst Interpretation over Documentary Facts). Class A shares hold most of the votes and the identities of holders, of the preferred holder and any related parties are not supplied (Insufficient Information). Key legal documents and every figure after June 30, 2026 are missing (Insufficient Information).

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In 2025 the company refinanced most of its term loans and its unsecured 2027 notes. On July 18, 2025 it issued 900 of 9.625% senior secured second lien notes due 2032 at par under an indenture of that date, and on December 12, 2025 it added 250 at 102% of par; interest is payable January 15 and July 15. On July 25, 2025 it issued 775 of 7.25% senior secured first lien notes due 2033 at par, payable February 15 and August 15. The second lien proceeds, with 50 borrowed under the revolver, were used to redeem the 2027 notes at par, repay 403 of the 2024 term loan, redeem 125 of the 10.5% first lien notes due 2029 at 103% of par, and pay expenses and for general purposes; the first lien proceeds repaid 630 of the 2021 term loan, 80 of the 2024 term loan and all 50 then drawn under the revolver. The revolver commitment was raised to 750 and extended to December 1, 2028 by the fifth amendment of July 18, 2025. The 2025 refinancing produced a loss on early extinguishment of debt of 10. The result is more secured debt with a later first maturity: second lien notes rank behind the credit agreement and both first lien note series, and all of these benefit from guarantees of substantially all subsidiaries and a pledge of substantially all assets excluding real estate.

In 2026 the company amended and restated its credit agreement on March 31, 2026 with no change in commitments, term loan principal or stated maturities and no new borrowings, repaid its remaining 2026 notes of 2 on January 20, 2026, and repaid the remaining 10 term loan balance on April 2, 2026. On June 30, 2026 it issued 70 of additional 7.25% first lien notes due 2033 at par in a private placement, using 40 for the first closing of the American Spirit Media purchase on July 1, 2026 and 30 to repurchase 50 of Series A preferred stock liquidation preference. On July 21, 2026 it repurchased 100 of its 2029 first lien notes and 20 of its 2031 notes at par plus accrued interest with cash and revolver borrowings. On August 6, 2026 the board authorized up to 250 of debt repurchases through December 31, 2027. The acquisitions that closed in the first half of 2026 were Bahakel's WBBJ-TV (25, license assets February 13, 2026), the Allen 3 (56, March 27, 2026), the Allen 7 (115, May 1, 2026), Block (80, May 6, 2026) and Sagamore Hill (2, May 8, 2026), plus a non-cash station swap with Scripps on May 15, 2026 recorded at a fair value of 70. The American Spirit Media (anticipated total 50) and WHPM (anticipated total 4) purchases had first closings on July 1, 2026; second closings are subject to regulatory approval and are not assured.

The creditor read-through is mixed and is labelled as analyst interpretation. First, secured debt grew and unsecured debt fell: first lien and second lien instruments now carry 65.8% of principal against 55.2% at December 31, 2024 (C3). Mechanism: new collateralised paper replaced unsecured notes and term loans, so unsecured claims rank behind more secured debt; the second lien tranche is itself junior to 2,709 of first lien debt. Second, the acquisitions were funded by cash that fell from 368 to 176 and by 70 of first lien debt, while the earnings contribution is only in the months after closing. Third, a debt repurchase program of up to 250 was authorised against liquidity of 921 and a fully drawn receivables facility, and the July repurchase drew on the revolver by an undisclosed amount. No sponsor, acquirer or merger is described. The company says "we anticipate that the WBBJ-TV acquisition will contribute to reducing our leverage" ([S-R-Feb page:3]); that is management language about one deal and station transactions announced in the second half of 2025, and no pro forma leverage is supplied.

fields.value: The financial base is a thinly covered, advertising-cyclical broadcaster that is usable for a snapshot only with its definitions kept apart. On issuer Adjusted EBITDA of 709 for the twelve months to June 30, 2026, principal debt of 5,867 is 8.28 times and debt net of cash is 8.03 times. The company's own covenant measure reads 5.73 times on net debt of 5,696 because its denominator is an eight-quarter average of 994 that includes the third and fourth quarters of the 2024 election year and acquisition, synergy and unrestricted-subsidiary adjustments. Both numbers are correct on their own basis; they must not be mixed, and neither is a maintenance test. The one maintenance covenant described is a first lien net leverage limit, which the issuer text ties to revolver borrowings or to more than 50 of uncollateralized letters of credit, with a stated cap of 4.25 times while revolver amounts are outstanding; the issuer reports 2.55 times at June 30, 2026.

Second, 2026 acquisitions add revenue and Adjusted EBITDA only from their closing dates, while the full acquisition cost and the July 2026 funding are already in debt or cash. Third, a 400 receivables securitization is fully drawn and sits outside reported debt principal, as does 600 of Series A perpetual preferred stock at liquidation value. Mechanism: retransmission consent revenue fell 50 in the first half of 2026 while network affiliation fees fell 61, so net retransmission revenue rose 11. fields.value: Gray Media is the largest owner of top-rated local television stations in the United States by its own description, with stations in 117 full-power markets at August 2026, a Telemundo affiliate group and a small production business. It earns money in three ways: core advertising that follows the economy and the audience, political advertising that arrives in even-numbered years and peaks in the fourth quarter, and retransmission consent fees paid by pay-television distributors, less the fees it pays to the four major networks. In FY2025 retransmission consent was 46% of revenue and core advertising 47%, with political at 1%; in FY2024, an election year, political was 14%. That structure gives the credit two features a creditor must read together: a large, contractual-looking fee stream that is shrinking in subscribers and exposed to blackouts and to network renewals through 2028, and a cyclical advertising stream whose largest swing is political.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The transaction story is a station-portfolio reshaping financed with debt and cash. In 2025 the company replaced term loans and unsecured notes with 1,150 of second lien notes and 775 of first lien notes, so that, after the January 2026 repayment of the last 2026 notes, no principal falls due before December 1, 2028. In 2026 it closed purchases from Allen Media Group, Block Communications, Sagamore Hill and Bahakel, swapped three stations to Scripps for two, amended and restated its credit agreement without changing commitments, issued 70 of additional first lien notes, repurchased 50 of preferred stock liquidation value for 30, and completed first closings of the American Spirit Media and WHPM purchases on July 1, 2026. Management says the WBBJ-TV acquisition and other station transactions will contribute to reducing leverage; the filings show the full acquisition cost is already in cash and debt while only part of the earnings is in the last twelve months. The context names no sponsor and the sources describe none: control runs through a dual-class common structure, and a senior preferred stock has a holder the pack does not name.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For a creditor the mechanism is straightforward. Political and retransmission revenue drive cash flow; acquisitions and refinancings drive leverage and the secured share of debt; Class A voting control and the preferred stock's change-of-control redemption shape who decides and who is paid first outside the debt. Documents that would show how much of this the creditor group can control, the credit agreement, indentures and purchase agreements, are not in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2025 the company refinanced most of its term loans and its unsecured 2027 notes. On July 18, 2025 it issued 900 of 9.625% senior secured second lien notes due 2032 at par under an indenture of that date, and on December 12, 2025 it added 250 at 102% of par; interest is payable January 15 and July 15. On July 25, 2025 it issued 775 of 7.25% senior secured first lien notes due 2033 at par, payable February 15 and August 15. The second lien proceeds, with 50 borrowed under the revolver, were used to redeem the 2027 notes at par, repay 403 of the 2024 term loan, redeem 125 of the 10.5% first lien notes due 2029 at 103% of par, and pay expenses and for general purposes; the first lien proceeds repaid 630 of the 2021 term loan, 80 of the 2024 term loan and all 50 then drawn under the revolver. The revolver commitment was raised to 750 and extended to December 1, 2028 by the fifth amendment of July 18, 2025. The 2025 refinancing produced a loss on early extinguishment of debt of 10. The result is more secured debt with a later first maturity: second lien notes rank behind the credit agreement and both first lien note series, and all of these benefit from guarantees of substantially all subsidiaries and a pledge of substantially all assets excluding real estate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2026 the company amended and restated its credit agreement on March 31, 2026 with no change in commitments, term loan principal or stated maturities and no new borrowings, repaid its remaining 2026 notes of 2 on January 20, 2026, and repaid the remaining 10 term loan balance on April 2, 2026. On June 30, 2026 it issued 70 of additional 7.25% first lien notes due 2033 at par in a private placement, using 40 for the first closing of the American Spirit Media purchase on July 1, 2026 and 30 to repurchase 50 of Series A preferred stock liquidation preference. On July 21, 2026 it repurchased 100 of its 2029 first lien notes and 20 of its 2031 notes at par plus accrued interest with cash and revolver borrowings. On August 6, 2026 the board authorized up to 250 of debt repurchases through December 31, 2027. The acquisitions that closed in the first half of 2026 were Bahakel's WBBJ-TV (25, license assets February 13, 2026), the Allen 3 (56, March 27, 2026), the Allen 7 (115, May 1, 2026), Block (80, May 6, 2026) and Sagamore Hill (2, May 8, 2026), plus a non-cash station swap with Scripps on May 15, 2026 recorded at a fair value of 70. The American Spirit Media (anticipated total 50) and WHPM (anticipated total 4) purchases had first closings on July 1, 2026; second closings are subject to regulatory approval and are not assured.

First, secured debt grew and unsecured debt fell: first lien and second lien instruments now carry 65.8% of principal against 55.2% at December 31, 2024 (C3). Second, the acquisitions were funded by cash that fell from 368 to 176 and by 70 of first lien debt, while the earnings contribution is only in the months after closing. Third, a debt repurchase program of up to 250 was authorised against liquidity of 921 and a fully drawn receivables facility, and the July repurchase drew on the revolver by an undisclosed amount. No sponsor, acquirer or merger is described. The company says "we anticipate that the WBBJ-TV acquisition will contribute to reducing our leverage" ([S-R-Feb page:3]); that is management language about one deal and station transactions announced in the second half of 2025, and no pro forma leverage is supplied.

fields.value: Gray Media is a stretched credit with adequate liquidity: the company has no principal maturity before December 2028, but it carries USD 5,867 million of debt against USD 709 million of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. Its strongest support is liquidity of USD 921 million and a maturity profile pushed out by the 2025 refinancing. Its weakest point is earnings coverage: debt is 8.28x Adjusted EBITDA, cash interest cover is 1.84x, and free cash flow after dividends is USD 59 million. What decides the outcome is whether 2026 election-year earnings and the acquired stations lift Adjusted EBITDA toward the USD 994 million denominator the company uses for its covenants, and whether retransmission renewals and the 2028 to 2031 refinancing are managed through the 2027 off-year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gray Media can service its debt and has time to refinance, but only if election-year earnings and acquired stations lift Adjusted EBITDA before 2028; on today's last-twelve-months earnings it is a highly levered credit with thin coverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gray Media's reported covenant leverage of 5.73x total net understates the burden shown by its own earnings. The company's covenant denominator is USD 994 million, an eight-quarter average that includes the third and fourth quarters of the 2024 election year and USD 144 million of acquisition, financing and synergy adjustments; its last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA is USD 709 million, and the same net debt of USD 5,696 million is 8.03x on that figure. Both are correct on their own bases and neither is a maintenance test. The mechanism is that incurrence capacity and covenant optics depend on a smoothed, pro forma denominator while cash interest of USD 385 million is paid out of actual earnings. This is Analyst Interpretation over CP-1 figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company's earnings are cyclical and its fee income is eroding at the same time. Retransmission consent was 46% of FY2025 revenue and political advertising 14% of FY2024 revenue and 1% of FY2025, and USD 133 million of the last twelve months; retransmission consent fell 4% in 2025 and 7% in the first half of 2026 on subscriber loss, one station going independent and a satellite blackout between March and May 1, 2026, with network affiliation fees falling faster so that net retransmission revenue rose to USD 292 million from USD 281 million. Network affiliation agreements expire between mid-2027 and December 31, 2028, just before the December 2028 term loan and revolver maturity. The implication is that FY2026 will flatter cash flow, and FY2027 and FY2028 carry the renewal and refinancing risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate but depleted by the 2026 transactions. Cash fell from USD 368 million to USD 176 million in the first half, after USD 264 million of acquisition spending; revolver availability is USD 745 million; and on July 21, 2026 the company repurchased USD 100 million of 2029 first lien notes and USD 20 million of 2031 notes using cash and an undisclosed revolver draw. Reading two issuer passages together, a first lien net leverage cap of 4.25x applies when the revolver is drawn or more than USD 50 million of letters of credit are uncollateralized; the company reports 2.55x, so a draw outstanding at a quarter-end would activate a test with headroom of about 40% of the denominator (Analyst Interpretation, issuer-described terms only).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The refinancing in 2025 moved debt up the structure. Principal secured by a lien rose to 65.4% of the total at December 31, 2025 and 65.8% at June 30, 2026, from 55.2% at December 31, 2024, with the 10.5% first lien notes due 2029 and the 9.625% second lien notes due 2032 carrying the highest coupons. Coupon arithmetic gives an annual cost of about USD 443 million on the instruments listed, against an issuer estimate of USD 465 million of interest payments over the next twelve months (the coupon sum excludes receivables-facility interest and fees). The implication for creditors is that unsecured noteholders hold USD 2,008 million behind USD 3,859 million of secured debt, and that the cost of debt leaves little earnings cushion; no recovery conclusion is drawn.

In the first half of 2026 the company paid USD 17 million of common dividends and USD 27 million of preferred dividends, and it used USD 30 million of new first lien debt to repurchase USD 50 million of preferred liquidation value at a USD 20 million discount. The issuer's USD 465 million interest estimate plus USD 83 million of guided 2026 dividends together equal 77.3% of last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA. fields.value: Strengths. Gray Media has scale: stations in 117 full-power markets reaching about 37% of US households, with its own count of 78 markets with the top-rated station (Management Language, Nielsen data not verified by the issuer). Its customer and market concentration is low: no advertiser above 5% of broadcast advertising and the largest market, Phoenix, at 5% of revenue (Documentary Fact). Its liquidity is USD 921 million and no principal is due before December 1, 2028, after refinancings that the company says extended maturities beyond the next two political cycles (Documentary Fact; the claim about political cycles is Management Language). The first lien net leverage ratio of 2.55x is well inside the 3.5x incurrence level and the 4.25x cap (Documentary Fact, issuer-reported). The company has reduced debt in the past: USD 520 million of net principal payments in 2024 (Documentary Fact). Net retransmission revenue held at USD 547 million in FY2025 against USD 550 million in FY2024 despite a USD 53 million fall in retransmission fees, because affiliation fees fell USD 50 million (Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Gray Media's leverage is 8.28x on last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA and 8.67x in FY2025, against 4.90x in FY2024, and cash interest cover is 1.84x (Documentary Fact, calculated). Its free cash flow is thin: USD 146 million before and USD 59 million after dividends over the last twelve months (calculated). Its earnings swing with the election cycle and with a high fixed-cost base, and Adjusted EBITDA is a release-only management measure (Documentary Fact). Its revenue base faces subscriber erosion and a cluster of affiliation expiries in 2027 and 2028 (Documentary Fact). A growing share of debt is secured, USD 400 million of receivables financing is fully drawn and outside reported debt, and USD 600 million of senior preferred stock carries a cash dividend of about USD 48 million a year and a change-of-control redemption (Analyst Interpretation over Documentary Facts). Class A shares hold most of the votes and the identities of holders, of the preferred holder and any related parties are not supplied (Insufficient Information). Key legal documents and every figure after June 30, 2026 are missing (Insufficient Information).
